question: A uniformly charged ring of radius $R$ carries a total positive charge $+Q$. The variation of electric potential $V$ along the ring’s axis (x-axis) is shown qualitatively in a graph. The center of the ring is at $x = 0$. The graph shows that $V(x)$ has a maximum value $V_0$ at $x = 0$, decreases smoothly as $|x|$ increases, and $V(x) \rightarrow 0$ as $x \rightarrow \pm\infty$. An electron is released from rest at a point A on the positive x-axis, very far from the ring ($V \approx 0$). It moves along the x-axis under the influence of the ring's electrostatic force. Using only the information from the graph, at which point along the x-axis will the speed of the electron be maximum?

options.A: At point A, very far from the ring
options.B: At some point between A and the center, but not at the center
options.C: At the center of the ring ($x = 0$) where $V = V_0$
options.D: The speed remains the same at all points along the axis
